version.changelog:
- Adds a major guidance section on migrating from legacy MEMORY.md and daily log memory to MemClaw, including detection instructions for AGENTS.md.
- Documents how session_id is determined, used, and mapped in memory storage, with updated usage examples.
- Clarifies default vs. per-session operation for all core tools and URIs.
- Updates all usage examples to use explicit or default session_id for clarity.
- No functional tool/API changes; documentation improvements and critical migration instructions only.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: memclaw
Version: 0.9.28

The memclaw skill provides a sophisticated tiered memory management system but includes high-risk instructions in SKILL.md that direct the AI agent to modify its own core configuration file (AGENTS.md) and perform plugin installations. While these actions are framed as a 'migration' from legacy memory systems, the ability to self-modify the agent's primary operating guidelines and install software constitutes a significant risk for persistence and unauthorized configuration changes. The tools also provide broad access to session history and user data via the cortex:// URI scheme, as detailed in references/memory-structure.md and references/tools.md.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions, requirements, and requested actions are coherent with a memory-plugin migration tool, but it will make persistent local configuration changes and the actual plugin code (fetched at install time) is not included for review — inspect the package and back up configs before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (a memory plugin) align with the content of SKILL.md: tools, URIs, migration, and storage locations are all memory-related. There are no unrelated environment variables or external credentials requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions include reading and modifying local OpenClaw configuration files (AGENTS.md, openclaw.json) and instruct the agent to run plugin management commands. That's reasonable for a migration/replace-memory task, but it's a persistent change to global agent configuration and the guidance gives the agent discretion to "assist in completing configurations," which is broader than purely read-only guidance.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill (no install spec or code included). The SKILL.md tells the user to run `openclaw plugins install @memclaw/memclaw`, which will fetch and install external code not present here — that means the actual executable/plugin behavior is outside this review and should be audited before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars or credentials. It does expect the user to configure LLM/embedding provider credentials in OpenClaw plugin settings (appropriate and proportional for a memory plugin). No requests for unrelated secrets are present in the skill content.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs modifications to user-level OpenClaw config (openclaw.json) and AGENTS.md to switch memory systems and to disable the built-in memory — these are persistent, cross-session changes. The skill is not marked always:true and does not autonomously escalate platform privileges, but it will alter global behavior if installed and configured.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This SKILL.md appears consistent with a memory-plugin migration tool, but the actual plugin code is not included here. Before installing: 1) Back up AGENTS.md and openclaw.json (the skill tells you to change them). 2) Inspect the @memclaw/memclaw package and its GitHub repo (https://github.com/sopaco/cortex-mem) to confirm there are no unexpected network calls or secret exfiltration. 3) Verify any local services the plugin expects (Qdrant on 6333/6334, cortex-mem-service on 8085) are ones you want running locally. 4) Be cautious when disabling built-in memory — test on a non-production agent first. 5) Monitor outgoing network connections after installation (the skill claims local-only processing but that cannot be verified from these files).
